titleText.es: Curiosidad de la Wikipedia: si eliges cualquier artículo y cliqueas en el primer enlace del artículo que no esté entre paréntesis o en cursiva, y repites el proceso, terminarás en
titleText.en: Wikipedia trivia: if you take any article, click on the first link in the article text not in parentheses or italics, and then repeat, you will eventually end up at "Philosophy".
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive title attribute is preserved exactly, including its truncated ending and trailing space; the official English title attribute is complete. The Spanish raster changes the final left-chat username from MIKE1979 to MIKE1970, a source anomaly preserved here. Vision omitted CALIBRE FIJO, ERROR, and the English article heading USAGE, confused several accents and letters, and emitted decorative browser/page strokes as false text. The clearly legible inherited English headings HISTORY and USAGE are inventoried as exclusions; tiny article-body and browser-interface squiggles are illustration rather than reliably readable writing.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A bujía creates the spark that ignites fuel in a petrol engine.

example.es: El mecánico revisó la bujía.
example.en: The mechanic checked the spark plug.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bujías is the plural of bujía.

example.es: El motor necesita bujías nuevas.
example.en: The engine needs new spark plugs.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In technical contexts, calibre can name a tool or standard used to check a dimension or gap.

example.es: Comprueba el espacio con un calibre.
example.en: Check the gap with a gauge.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Fijo describes something that stays set rather than changing.

example.es: El aparato mantiene un ritmo fijo.
example.en: The device keeps a fixed rhythm.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Recarga tells one familiar person to load a page or resource again.

example.es: Recarga la página dentro de un minuto.
example.en: Reload the page in a minute.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Conectar can describe establishing a technical link between systems.

example.es: No puedo conectar el ordenador con la red.
example.en: I cannot connect the computer to the network.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: After conectar, con can introduce the system or service at the other end of the connection.

example.es: La aplicación conecta con el servidor.
example.en: The application connects to the server.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Base combines with de datos to form the common technical term base de datos.

example.es: La base de datos está disponible.
example.en: The database is available.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: After a form of haber, cambiado presents cambiar as completed. With a car part, it often means replaced.

example.es: He cambiado el filtro del coche.
example.en: I have replaced the car's filter.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: runs; is running (a vehicle or machine)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A vehicle or machine that va bien or va mal is running well or badly.

example.es: El coche va bien después de la reparación.
example.en: The car runs well after the repair.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Separación can mean the measured space between two parts.

example.es: Mide la separación entre las piezas.
example.en: Measure the gap between the parts.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Correcta agrees with a feminine singular noun.

example.es: Esa es la medida correcta.
example.en: That is the correct measurement.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Electrodos are conductors through which electric current enters or leaves a material or device.

example.es: Los electrodos están separados.
example.en: The electrodes are separated.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to see it; to check it
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Verlo combines ver with lo, which stands for a masculine thing or an idea already mentioned.

example.es: Puedes verlo con una lupa.
example.en: You can check it with a magnifying glass.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Motor can refer to the engine that powers a vehicle or machine.

example.es: El motor funciona con gasolina.
example.en: The engine runs on petrol.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Del combines de + el. After depender, de introduces the factor that determines the result.

example.es: La fecha depende del tiempo.
example.en: The date depends on the weather.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; introduces the person or thing affected
cardDefinitions.noteEn: When le or les already marks an affected person or thing before the verb, a can introduce a later phrase that makes that person or thing explicit. Natural English may instead use a possessive form or a word such as ‘on.’

example.es: Le cambié la rueda a la bicicleta.
example.en: I changed the bicycle's wheel.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Caerse can describe a website, network, or service becoming unavailable.

example.es: Cuando se cae la red, esperamos.
example.en: When the network goes down, we wait.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Caer can describe a number, level, score, or apparent ability decreasing.

example.es: La temperatura cae por la noche.
example.en: The temperature drops at night.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Aparente describes how something seems, which may differ from what it really is.

example.es: Su calma aparente ocultaba los nervios.
example.en: His apparent calm hid his nerves.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something connects to a system or service?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use conectar con, followed by that system or service.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The form of conectar can change for tense or person; con introduces the other endpoint.

example.es: El programa intenta conectar con el servidor.
example.en: The program tries to connect to the server.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the standard Spanish term for a database?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The plural datos stays plural inside this fixed technical term.

example.es: Guardamos la información en una base de datos.
example.en: We store the information in a database.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does the outage make the same person suddenly seem much less intelligent?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: He was using Wikipedia as external memory, so losing access removes the knowledge he had appeared to possess.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The left chat shows detailed car advice supported by open Wikipedia tabs. When Wikipedia fails, the right chat cannot identify even a spark plug or a car. The caption treats that dependence as an extended-mind joke: a tool outside the brain temporarily functions like part of the person's knowledge. CI is the Spanish abbreviation for intelligence quotient.
